agent_notes: This change tightens SSRF validation. It adds multicast blocking and unwraps IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses before checking them. Nothing it newly blocks (multicast, or ::ffff: forms of loopback, link-local, unspecified or multicast addresses) is a valid *arr server endpoint, so it does not reject any URL the input contract supports.

The explicit `ipv4_mapped` unwrap behaves the same on every Python version. From Python 3.13, CPython also makes IPv6Address properties defer to the mapped IPv4 address, so on 3.13+ the new branch is partly redundant but harmless. On 3.11/3.12 (the project minimum is 3.11) it is what makes the block work.

Only re-saving that URL through the settings form would be rejected, with 'Blocked address'.
No schema, migration or persistence changes. Performance cost is a few attribute lookups per form submit, which is negligible.

Verdict: shippable as-is. The two findings describe existing gaps that the diff leaves unchanged; neither is a regression.
